newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures ends down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures ends down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply down in active trading on Monday due to last Friday's losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
The most actively traded October 1997 contract ended at 23,010 yuan ($2,774) per tonne, losing 380 yuan.
It opened at 23,180 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 23,200 yuan and a low of 22,980 yuan per tonne.
July fell 180 to 22,600, August 210 to 22,760, September 280 to 22,890, November 430 to 23,080, and December 430 to 23,100.
Combined volume rose sharply to 82,200 tonnes from 20,210.
Copper opened sharply lower and fell further before closing at or near intraday lows, traders said.
LME copper failed to breach the key $2,600 resistance level early in Friday trading. It ended near the day's low at $2,567 a tonne, compared to Thursday's $2,585.50.

LME copper was expected to remain sensitive to developments at the long-running strike at Inco's Sudbury facilities, with traders continuing to prepare for another spell of tightness as the cash/three months backwardation sat at $127.
Shanghai traders said market sentiment was greatly weakened by the LME losses and few investors wanted to buy.
"Large amounts of stop-loss selling orders emerged on the market in the morning session, indicating many investors were disappointed at the LME performance," one trader said.
"Technical charts will be more unfriendly to long position holders after today's sharp falls," he added.
Physical prices in the Shanghai area fell to 22,600-22,650 yuan due to heavy losses on the futures market, traders said.
Traders said copper was likely to maintain current levels over coming days unless there was some market-moving news.
"Late-maturing contracts found support at the 23,000-yuan level on Monday and it will be difficult to breach this level if there is no fresh negative news," a second trader said.
Aluminium futures ended down sharply, following copper's trend, traders said.
July fell 250 to 14,050, August 150 to 14,150, September 190 to 14,310 and October 170 to 14,480 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 2,000 tonnes from 450 tonnes.
